newsitem.title: JORDAN: HSBC holds Jordan bond roadshow next week.
newsitem.headline: HSBC holds Jordan bond roadshow next week.

text.p: London-based HSBC Markets will launch an investor roadshow in Bahrain, Geneva and London next week to promote Jordan's first corporate $100 million eurobond, issued by Jordan Phosphate Mines Company (JPMC).

Ziad al-Basha, head of securities at Jordan's subsidiary of British Bank of the Middle East, part of the HSBC group, said the show would kick off next Sunday in Bahrain, to be followed on July 15 in Geneva and later in London during July 17-19.

Basha said it will be followed later in the month or early August by an official ceremony by the phosphate company to award HSBC the mandate to jointly lead manage the issue with Jordan's Arab Bank. The floating of the bond issue was expected by first week of August.
Local banks will play a significant role in the issue after Arab Bank formed a syndicate with them to underwrite as a much as 50 percent of the issue.
"The Jordanian market took $50 million and we could sell more to the local market," said Mifleh Aqel, regional manager of Arab Bank.

HSBC Markets was picked from seven bidders shortlisted for the $100 million five-year floating rate note (FRN), the country's first corporate bond issue, by Jordan Phosphate Mines with the guidance of Jordan Central Bank and the World Bank.
Jordan Phosphate Mines Company wants to tap international markets to partly finance an estimated $250 million project to expand its major Shidiyah mine.

Banking sources say the mandate was awarded on the lowest bid for the offer, around 1.5 percent or 150 basis points above LIBOR, but HSBC sources insist the final pricing is subject to the investor roadshow.
The bond issue has already attracted much attention and HSBC envisage few problems in marketing the issue in capital markets.
"This is a good story to tell and we expect the issue will be well received by Gulf financial institutions, global investors and private high net individuals," Basha said.

HSBC, in its latest research paper on Jordan, has favourably upgraded the kingdom's credit worthiness saying "there was a visible improvement in credit worthiness which shows through two ratios - external debt over export or over GDP."
